notes: Device registrations: where each device's TOOL TIP is, expressed in the axis
space of the device the camera rides on (ref_device). Given a pose h on the
registered device, its tip is at  p_ref = R * h + offset  -- and the pose that
puts the tip at a point is  h = R^T * (p_ref - offset).
Everything is in RAW AXIS coordinates of the two named devices. This is the
same rule the needle offset follows and for the same reason: a pick already
reports there, read_position reads there, move_axis_to commands there, and
gantry-main's entry in motion_transforms.json inverts Z - so a number that
took a detour through the axis transform would descend where it meant to
retreat.
R IS MEASURED, NOT COPIED FROM motion_transforms.json. That file's matrices
are hand-typed permutations of +-1; they are exact for a device bolted square
and quietly wrong for one that is not, in a way that predicts perfectly at the
point it was taught and misses by a millimetre 30 mm away. The typed matrix is
used only to AIM the camera during the measurement.
This file SHIPS EMPTY. There is nothing sensible to seed: unlike the needle,
where a tape measure gets the first imprint into frame, the aiming seed here
is derived from motion_transforms.json automatically. Run the registration
procedure (Registration page, F8) on each device that carries a tool.
A completed registration is written to config/device_reg.local.json, which is
gitignored and loads in preference to this file. Do not hand-edit that one -
the Registration page shows it, re-measures it, and checks it.
Two dates, and the difference matters: registered_at is the four-pick fit of R
and offset; tip_taught_at is the last time offset alone was re-measured. R
belongs to the MOUNT, offset belongs to the mount AND the tool - so changing a
gripper invalidates one pick's worth of the record, not the whole thing.
